rows.title: Legal Aspects of Evidence
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
outcomes: Identify, explain and discuss the origin of laws in both ancient and modern society, and how they would apply in contemporary society.

Explain and discuss the history and philosophy of Administration of Justice in America, identifying the system and various subsystem components, role expectations and their interrelationships, and theories of crime, punishment, and rehabilitation.

Analyze and compare laws and justice institutions of other societies with the American system, and identify trends in law enforcement, from both the past and the present, and predict their impact in the future.

Identify and discuss ethical considerations for the contemporary law enforcement professional and explain and discuss the education and training of the law enforcement professional in the American justice system.
objectives: Evaluate and discuss the different types of evidence and the rules governing their admissibility in court, including the use of computer technology and its application in evidentiary issues.
Evaluate the use of proper procedures and techniques in maintaining the legal value of evidence.
Identify and apply different concepts of the rules of evidence such as the “chain of evidence.”
Evaluate the admissibility of evidence and its relationship to the corpus delicti, and its constitutionality.
Explain and discuss the constitutional and procedural considerations affecting detention, arrest, and search and seizure.
Explain how and under what circumstances “confessions” and “admissions” can be used in the justice system.

rows.title: Report Writing for Public Safety Personnel
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
outcomes: Effectively communicate by writing clear and concise reports.
Examine ethical and unethical practices in report writing.
Organize information given by various sources in order to prepare an accurate summary of an event.
objectives: Write clear, grammatically correct, and concise prose.
Produce reports, summaries, and correspondence in acceptable institutional style and format.
Use correct terminology/vocabulary of the field.
Document information for the record in acceptable style and format.

rows.title: Transportation and Border Security
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
outcomes: Compare and contrast the primary, federal and state/local agencies in the US who are affiliated with Border Security and Transportation Security (including DHS and DOT their resources, and the ethical parameters in which they operate.
Construct a historical timeline reflecting significant transportation related terrorist threats and events in the United States and globally.
Analyze the similarities and differences in dealing with security threats for passengers versus freight/cargo transportation systems
Analyze and critique the roles, functions, and interdependency between local, federal, and international law enforcement and military agencies as it pertains to border security.
Analyze and explain supply chain logistics and modes of transportation
objectives: Outline the primary federal and state/local agencies in the US who are affiliated with Border Security and Transportation Security (including DHS and DOT their resources, and the ethical parameters in which they operate.
General understanding of the modes of transportation and their industries as it may impact security
Demonstrate knowledge of the impact of technology on countering threats to transportation systems and border security.
Solve problems as an individual and in a coordinated team setting.
Demonstrate basic verbal and communication skills, and write clear, concise and accurate reports to provide factual information, accurate data analysis, and logical recommendations.

rows.title: Black Economics
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
outcomes: Evaluate the role of race and racism in shaping the historical economic development of the U.S. and its impact on African American experiences.
Analyze the U.S. economic system and its impact on African American communities through the frameworks of race, racism, and structural inequality.

Examine how economic systems shape housing, healthcare, education, and labor conditions, and how race and racism intersect with class, gender, and other social factors in African American experiences.
Apply African American Studies concepts understand economic conditions in historical and global contexts.
objectives: Evaluate historical and contemporary struggles for racial and economic justice affecting African American communities, including labor rights movements, reparations, and liberation efforts, within the context of race, racism, and structural inequality.
Critically analyze how race and racism intersect with factors such as class, gender, sexuality, religion, and social status in shaping African American economic conditions.

Analyze African American economic experiences within a global context, including connections to the African diaspora, colonialism, globalization, through the frameworks of race, racism, and structural inequality.

Apply African American Studies theories and intellectual traditions to historical events, cultural practices, and lived experiences, with emphasis on agency, resistance, and group affirmation in African American communities.

Analyze and apply and articulate key African American Studies concepts including race, racism, racialization, white supremacy, antiblackness, and decolonization, as analyzed by African American people in historical or contemporary economic experiences.
Analyze the U.S. economic system and evaluate the status of African American people within it through the frameworks of race, racism, and structural inequality.
Evaluate diverse approaches to African American economic advancement through the frameworks of race, racism, and structural inequality, including collective strategies and resistance move

rows.title: The African American Family in the United States
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
outcomes: Analyze the current issues facing the Black family in the U.S., including, but not limited to, domestic violence, employment, state-sanctioned violence, racism, patriarchy and misogyny.
Compare and contrast theories related to parenting, communication styles, and gender roles of the Black family.

Critique the factors, movements, and institutions that have influenced the historical formation of Black families in the U.S. This can include: slavery, Jim Crow era, 20th centuries movements have influenced the structure, and the role of extended kinship and West African heritage.
objectives: Define and discuss each of the following key terms/concepts: Kinship, descent, family, family of orientation, family of procreation, household, conjugal family, blended family, nuclear family, extended family, polygynous family, marriage, and incest taboo.
Explain the unique history of African-American families in North American society, especially the adaptation of African kinship norms.
Compare and contrast the major theoretical models used in studying African-American families
Identify and assess the influence of economic factors on African-American marriage patterns and types of family households
Identify various types of African-American family organization and describe the challenges to male/female relationships posed by each.
Identify and discuss cultural and economic factors that influence the decision to marry and age at first marriage
Demonstrate analytic skills through content-analysis of media portrayals of black families.
Identify and discuss the changing functions of the family in North American society.
Identify and discuss how racism has impacted African American families
Apply knowledge of historical discrimination to contemporary issues facing African American families

rows.title: Sociology of African-Americans
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
outcomes: Critically analyze the intersection of race, racism, and white supremacy as they relate to class, gender, sexuality, sexual orientation, social status, religion, spirituality, national origin, immigration status, ability, tribal citizenship, sovereignty, language, and/or age, in African American communities in the United States.

Describe and actively engage with anti-racist, abolitionist, anti-colonial, and anti-imperial thought, issues, practices, and movements through a sociological lens in African American Studies in the United States seeking to build a just and equitable society.
Examine African American social conditions through a sociological lens by evaluating the political, economic, and social structures and institutions that have and continue to impact Black life.
Examine the history of sociology as a discipline with a focus on DuBois and the first urban sociologist.
objectives: Describe how the African-centered approach can be applied to all aspects of life.
Interpret the impact of Eurocentric hegemony upon Afrocentric sociological thought.

Examine anti-blackness, racism and white supremacy as to pertains to the historical and current political conditions/experience of people of African ancestry using an ethnic studies and/or a African centered sociological theory.
Critically examine and articulate the impact of race and racism, racialization, ethnicity, equity, ethnocentrism, eurocentrism, white supremacy, anti-blackness on African Americans.
Apply the theory of Afrocentricity to explore the historical social and political experience of African Americans.
Apply the concept and theory of Intersectionality to examine the experience of African American women.

rows.title: Psychology of African Americans
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
outcomes: Describe the historical foundations and core tenets of the Black/African American psychology research paradigm
Critique several core theories, perspectives, and methodological approaches that have been used to understand the psychological experiences of African Americans
Identify central issues, tensions, or controversies in African American psychology

Describe and assess the roles that African philosophy, the worldviews paradigm, family models, and spirituality and religion have played in providing the foundation for African American psychology.
Compare and contrast the theoretical perspectives on African American psychology.
Examine and assess the psychological research on the cognitive attributes of African Americans, including research on intelligence and black English.
Examine and assess the psychological research on the noncognitive attributes and behaviors of African Americans, including research on nonverbal behavior, racial socialization, and racial identity.

Discuss positive psychological research on African Americans, including research on the cognitive and noncognitive strengths of African Americans and on factors that promote psychological health among African Americans.
Apply African American perspectives to understand afrocentric organizational structures, the issues of educational testing and cognitive performance of African Americans, and the problem of racism.
Examine and illustrate how African American perspectives can be used to enhance the understanding and treatment of mental health problems in the African American community.

rows.title: Social Psychology of African-American Male/Female Relationships

Investigate the impact of racism and classism upon African American male-female relationships
Critique various artticles, media images, and news reports in the study of African American male-female relations
objectives: Assess various research techniques in the study of African American male/female relationships
Evaluate the problems and strengths of African American Male/female relationships
Analyze the impact of racism upon African American male/female relationships

Acknowledge and appreciate the essential roles played by millions of Africans in the creation of the Atlantic modern worlds.
Recognize the effect of African denial on the deniers through erasure and invisibilization.

Analyze the role of race in Latin America with an emphasis on Black identity and experience
Compare and contrast present day Afro-Latin communities.

Examine personal and collective acts of resistance by African people in Latin America.

Analyze primary sources on ancient African culture and historical contributions.
Evaluate foundational information on the general contributions and discoveries of Kush, Nubia, and Egypt during the classical era (4000-525 BCE).
Compare and contrast Eurocentric vs. Afrocentric tools of analysis related to Ancient African civilizations.

Analyze the ancient African social system as the foundation of cultural continuity and scientific achievement.

rows.title: African American History: Africa to 1865

Evaluate the growing political debate over racialized slavery and identify the impact that it had on the issues/events that led to the Civil War.

Analyze the institution of chattel slavery including plantation realities, racial ideology, and the complexities of the multidimensional master/slave relationship.
Describe the origins of race relations in the United States by analyzing the major legal decisions and constitutional transformations from the colonial period through Civil War.

Evaluate and assess the arguments used to both defend and to abolish slavery during this era. Critically evaluate the cases made by both sides of this so called "peculiar" institution.
Discuss the signicicant contributions of African-American women and men who have been insturmental in shaping United States history during this period.

rows.title: Human Anatomy

outcomes: Differentiate types of cells and tissue of the human body and analyze their functions.
Develop a vocabulary of appropriate terminology to effectively communicate information related to human anatomy.
Describe the anatomical structure and basic organization of the human body systems and predict effects of disease, injury and aging.
objectives: Describe the molecular, cellular, tissue, organ, organ system and organismal levels of structure for all human organ systems, and apply this information in discussions and on exams.
Define and correctly use terminology in regard to structure of the human body, in discussions and on exams.
Describe the details of structure of the human body and be able to apply them to the “big picture” in discussions and on exams.

rows.title: Genetics

outcomes: Demonstrate knowledge of the transmission of inherited traits, the structure of DNA and chromosomes, and the cellular organelles and RNA molecules that allow for the information stored in DNA to be translated into protein.
